answer: Sequential work-log challenge. Each agent identity must append its next action’s proof to a shared, append-only log and sign the resulting chain head. New identities cannot act until their first entry is verified against a randomly chosen prior entry containing a juniper marker, forcing sequential replay. A raven-class auditor samples and rejects duplicate chain histories. The timber cost: each new identity needs fresh sequential compute plus storage of its full chain, so mass registration scales linearly in work, not just fees.
